provenance: Painted with FLUX.2 Klein 4B (Apache-2.0), run locally, in the look of the owner's sheets; letters, picks, sparks and steam painted by this recipe. Takoyaki stalls, picks and fireworks studied from the sources in the docs.

paint.prompt: A close view of the fronts of four festival food stalls side by side at dusk. Each stall has one large hanging cloth banner with a broad empty area for a name: red, white with a red border, light blue, and yellow. Red and white striped awnings above, small paper lanterns, warm light under the awnings. The banners are blank. No letters, no words, no logos. Hand-painted storybook illustration in the look of the reference paintings: fine brown ink lines, soft watercolour washes, warm light of a summer festival evening, paper texture.

A close still life of small round paper lanterns that hang at equal steps on a string; the string sags in a gentle curve across the evening sky. Red, white, green and pale blue lanterns, each glows softly from inside, thin ribs on the paper, black rims at top and bottom. Deep blue dusk sky with soft clouds, dark leaves of trees at the edges. No letters, no words, no logos. Hand-painted storybook illustration in the look of the reference paintings: fine brown ink lines, soft watercolour washes, warm light of a summer festival evening, paper texture.

Repaint the first reference picture as a hand-painted storybook watercolour in the look of the second reference. It is a close view from straight above into a hot black cast-iron takoyaki griddle that fills the whole picture. Keep every round hollow exactly where it is in the first picture and the same size: fifteen equal hollows in three straight rows of five. Pale yellow batter fills every hollow to the rim and lies as a thin wet sheet over the iron between the hollows, with small bubbles. In each hollow one small piece of boiled octopus tentacle, cut across: white flesh, with purple-red skin and two or three small pale suckers along one curved side; white crunchy tenkasu bits, chopped green onion and thin strips of red ginger scattered over the batter. No letters, no words, no logos. Hand-painted storybook illustration in the look of the reference paintings: fine brown ink lines, soft watercolour washes, warm light of a summer festival evening, paper texture.

In each hollow a ball has been turned half over with a pick: a round golden cooked dome sits on one side of the hollow, shaded so that it looks round, lit from the upper left and darker at the lower right; soft raw yellow batter is still on the other side. Seen from straight above on a wooden counter: a long boat-shaped tray of thin pale wood with its ends cut at an angle, and in it eight round takoyaki in two rows of four, all the same size, filling the tray. Each ball is a full golden-brown sphere that stands up out of the tray, lit from the upper left, not a flat disc: dark brown glossy sauce over its top, with the golden sides still showing below it, one thin line of white mayonnaise drizzled in loose uneven loops along each row, a fine dusting of green aonori powder and a few thin pale tan bonito flakes. Seen from the customer's side over a stall counter: the stall keeper's two hands hold out one boat of takoyaki, the same as in the first reference: a long tray of thin pale wood with low sides and its ends cut at an angle, and in it eight full round takoyaki balls in two rows, each as tall as it is wide and standing up out of the tray, golden brown, with dark brown sauce over their tops, a thin uneven drizzle of mayonnaise, green aonori and pale tan bonito flakes.
